findings.title: Embed highlights template is invalid Ruby and 500s
findings.body: `<%- end if %>` is compiled as Ruby `end if`, which is a syntax error (a block `if` is closed with `end`, not `end if`). ERB turns the whole template into one method, so any render of `embed/best` raises SyntaxError before HTML is produced. The first visit can still show `loading.html.erb` and enqueue a retrieve; once a `topic_embeds` row exists, every later iframe load 500s and the discussion never appears. The new controller spec does not enable `render_views`, so it never compiles this template and stays green.

findings.title: Imported HTML is stored raw and executed on the Discourse origin
findings.body: RSS items and remotely fetched pages are saved with `cook_method: raw_html` and `skip_validations: true`. `Post#cook` then returns `raw` unchanged, and both the embed view (`raw post.cooked`) and the normal topic UI render `cooked` as HTML. Nothing runs the content through Sanitize. `ruby-readability` 0.5.7 does not honor the `tags:` / `attributes:` arguments passed in `import_remote` (those are Sanitize-style options and are ignored), so scripts, event handlers, and `javascript:` links from the remote page are kept. `PollFeed` also `CGI.unescapeHTML`s the feed body first, turning entity-encoded markup into live tags. Separately, line 13 interpolates the source URL into a single-quoted `href` and into the link text with no encoding; `absolutize_urls` reparses with Nokogiri, which preserves injected elements and handlers. A feed link or embed URL such as `http://example.com/' onclick='alert(1)` becomes an active handler in the stored post. A normal CMS feed that includes an embed script is enough; the script runs as the viewing user on the forum origin, including inside the embed iframe.

findings.title: Feed polling crashes on ordinary RSS items
findings.body: `i.content.scrub` assumes every item has a string `content` and that `String#scrub` exists. Standard RSS 2.0 only has `description` (SimpleRSS sets `content` from `content:encoded`), so `i.content` is nil and this raises NoMethodError on the first such item. `String#scrub` itself was added in Ruby 2.1, so on Ruby 2.0/1.9 the call fails even when content is present. There is no per-item rescue, and `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so one bad item aborts the rest of the feed until the next hour. `TopicRetriever` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute` inline before the HTTP fallback, so the same exception also skips `import_remote` for the URL the user actually asked to embed. `feed_key` is computed and never used, and `open` is not given a timeout or closed.

findings.title: Resize postMessage never arrives in the parent
findings.body: `parent.postMessage(..., request.referer)` passes the full referer URL (scheme, host, path, and query) as `targetOrigin`. Browsers of this era compare that argument to the parent's origin (`https://host`), not to the full page URL, and drop the message when they differ. `<%= request.referer %>` is also HTML-escaped, so a referer containing `&` is inserted as `&` and cannot match even in browsers that parse `targetOrigin` as a URL. `embed.js` creates the iframe with `scrolling="no"` and no height, and only grows it on `discourse-resize`. The message is discarded, so the iframe stays at the default ~150px and comments are clipped with no scrollbar.

findings.title: Resize listener treats any prefix of the forum URL as a trusted origin
findings.body: The check is `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`, i.e. whether the forum URL string contains the sender origin, not whether the sender equals the forum origin. Any origin that is a string prefix of `discourseUrl` is accepted. For a forum at `https://discuss.example.com`, an attacker origin of `https://discuss.example.co` matches because `"https://discuss.example.com".indexOf("https://discuss.example.co") === 0`. That window can set `iframe.height` to an arbitrary value. Combined with `scrolling="no"`, a huge height covers the embedding page with the iframe. The listener also does not require `e.source === iframe.contentWindow`.

findings.title: import_remote fetches the embed URL with open-uri and follows redirects
findings.body: `import_remote` does `open(url).read` with no `require 'open-uri'` in this file (only `poll_feed.rb` requires it), no read size limit, no timeout, and no close. Unless some other file has already loaded open-uri, `Kernel#open` treats the URL as a local path and raises Errno::ENOENT, so the non-RSS embed path never imports. When open-uri is loaded, it follows HTTP redirects. `TopicRetriever` only compares the original URL's host to `embeddable_host`, so `http://allowed-host/redirect` that 302s to `http://127.0.0.1`, link-local cloud metadata, or another internal service is fetched and then stored as a public topic via the raw_html path. The embed action enqueues that fetch for any client that can set `Referer` to the allowed host. The same method is also called from the Disqus importer with links taken from the XML, with no host allowlist. Failures are unrescued, so a 404, SSL error, or huge body fails the job.

findings.title: embed_url is varchar(255) under a unique index
findings.body: `t.string :embed_url` is a varchar(255) on PostgreSQL, and the unique index is on that column. Article URLs with long slugs or tracking query strings routinely exceed 255 characters. `TopicEmbed.create!` then raises a string-right-truncation error, the import transaction rolls back, and that article can never be embedded. The column needs to be `text` (or a much larger limit); a unique btree index on text is valid in PostgreSQL.

findings.title: Disqus import drops threads when the live page cannot be fetched
findings.body: Topic creation used to be a local `PostCreator` call with the export title, `created_at`, permalink body, and optional `-c` category. It now depends entirely on `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which GETs `t[:link]` and returns nil on any network, HTTP, or readability failure. The comment loop is inside `if post.present?`, so a dead or blocked link silently skips every comment on that thread. `import_remote` / `TopicEmbed.import` also have no `created_at` or category argument, and the `-c` / `--category` option was removed, so existing invocations that passed a category fail and imported topics are dated now in the default category instead of the original thread date and destination.

findings.title: Bulk embed imports still hit create rate limiters
findings.body: `skip_validations: true` only turns off ActiveRecord validations. `Post` still includes `RateLimiter::OnCreateRecord` (`rate_limit` / `rate_limit_create_post`, plus topic creation limits in `TopicCreator`), and those callbacks run on save. A feed or retrieve that creates more than a handful of topics in one run will raise `RateLimiter::LimitExceeded` or roll back mid-loop; `PollFeed` has no per-item rescue, so the rest of the feed is skipped until the limit window resets (`max_topics_per_day` is 20). The Disqus task in this same change calls `RateLimiter.disable` around its import loop; `PollFeed` and `TopicRetriever` do not. Updates pass `bypass_rate_limiter`, but that flag only skips `EditRateLimiter` inside `PostRevisor`, not create limits.

findings.title: Every embed miss re-downloads and imports the entire feed
findings.body: When `feed_polling_enabled?` is set, each cache miss calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute` synchronously inside the retrieve job, before the single-URL HTTP fetch. The Redis throttle key is per embed URL, not per feed, so ten different articles trigger ten full feed downloads and imports per minute, on top of the hourly schedule (this path does not take the scheduler lock, so it can overlap the hourly run). `PollFeed#feed_key` looks like a conditional-GET / already-seen short-circuit but is never read, and `poll_feed` always `open`s the feed URL and walks every item. One slow or huge feed blocks the worker and can create a topic for every item as a side effect of viewing a single embed.

findings.title: Retrieve throttle can stick forever if expire does not run
findings.body: `retrieved_recently?` does `SETNX retrieved:<url> 1` and only then `EXPIRE 60`. Those are not atomic. If the process dies, Redis errors, or expire is skipped between the two calls, the key has no TTL. `retrieved_recently?` then stays true for that exact URL forever (unless `no_throttle` is set for staff), so the article is never fetched again. Use a single `SET key 1 NX EX 60` (or set the TTL inside the same command the deployment's Redis supports). The same gap exists for every distinct embed URL.

findings.title: Embed URLs are compared exactly, so the same article splits or is skipped
findings.body: Lookup, uniqueness, and the import short-circuit all use the raw URL string (`where(embed_url: url)` and the unique index). There is no normalization: `http://host/a` and `http://host/a/`, a URL with a fragment or `utm_*` query, and the same path with a different scheme case are different rows, so one article becomes multiple topics. The allowlist check is also case-sensitive: `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` uses `URI(embed_url).host`, which preserves case (`Example.COM`), and compares it to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` with `!=`. `TopicEmbed.import` only accepts URLs matching `/^https?:\/\//`, so `HTTP://...` is dropped. `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` uses the same case-sensitive host compare on `Referer`. Mixed-case canonical URLs from a CMS or feed never import, and the loading iframe retries forever.

findings.title: Deleting the topic or first post leaves a row that crashes embed and feed updates
findings.body: `belongs_to :topic` / `:post` do not declare `dependent: :destroy`, and `Topic` is not given a matching association, so destroying a topic or its first post leaves `topic_embeds` in place (there is also no foreign key). The embed action then does `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` for a missing topic and 500s on every view instead of importing again. On the next feed change, `post = embed.post` is nil and `PostRevisor.new(post)` raises, which aborts the rest of `PollFeed`'s item loop. `import` also treats any in-memory `PostCreator` result as success (`post.present?` is true for an unsaved post after a rolled-back create) and will `create!` an embed pointing at a topic id that was never committed.

findings.title: Anyone who can set Referer can enqueue unbounded outbound fetches
findings.body: `ensure_embeddable` only compares `Referer`'s host to `embeddable_host`. That header is not a credential; any client can send `Referer: http://<embeddable_host>/` and GET `/embed/best?embed_url=...`. On a cache miss the action always `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic)` with the caller-supplied URL and no per-IP or global limit. The job's 60s Redis throttle is per exact URL, so many distinct paths on the allowed host become many Sidekiq jobs and many outbound requests (and, after redirects, internal ones). `loading.html.erb` reloads every 30 seconds and enqueues again. `TopicRetriever` returns quietly on host mismatch, blank `embed_by_username`, throttle, or fetch failure, but the UI has no error state, so a misconfiguration or attacker page keeps scheduling work forever. This is a GET that mutates server state (jobs and topics), so crawlers and prefetch can trigger it too when a matching referer is present.

findings.title: absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs and skips other relative ones
findings.body: The helper claims to absolutize relative URLs but only rewrites `a[href]` and `img[src]` that `start_with?('/')`. A protocol-relative URL such as `//cdn.example.com/a.png` matches that check, then `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both slashes, so it is rewritten to `http://<article-host>/cdn.example.com/a.png` instead of keeping the CDN host. Relative URLs that do not start with `/` (`images/a.png`, `../a.png`, `?page=2`) are left unchanged and later resolve against the Discourse origin, so images and links 404 or hit forum routes. Both forms are common in RSS and article HTML. Only root-relative paths like `/hello` work, which is the only case the new spec covers.

findings.title: import mutates contents in place and crashes when the body is nil
findings.body: `contents << footer` appends to the caller's string instead of copying it. `import_remote` passes `doc.content` through, and Readability returns nil when it cannot extract an article, so this raises NoMethodError and the retrieve job fails (the loading iframe then retries forever). A frozen string raises the same way. Callers that reuse the buffer also get a second footer and a different SHA1 on the next import. Build a new string (`"#{contents}#{footer}"`) after rejecting blank content.

findings.title: Embed controller spec never renders the templates it claims succeed
findings.body: The success examples do not call `render_views` (rspec-rails 2 stubs views by default), so they never compile `best.html.erb` and cannot catch the `end if` syntax error. The example that expects a topic view stubs `TopicView.new` without a return value; mocha yields nil, so `@topic_view` is nil and a real render would raise before the `after` hook's `response.should be_success`. `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only stubs whether `execute` calls `poll_feed` and never parses a feed, so the nil-`content` crash and unsanitized import are also untested.
